corrections.text: The article states, "The model was newly trained to target forecasts to specific weather stations, which Google says produces more granular predictions and lets researchers evaluate results against ground-truth data," attributing this to Google's blog post. Google's blog does not make this claim; it says only that the model "trains directly on sparse weather station observation data" for topography-aware gridded forecasts. The claim about targeting forecasts to specific weather stations for granular predictions and ground-truth evaluation is TechCrunch's reporting: "the designers also trained the model to target its forecasts to specific weather data stations... for offering more granular predictions... and evaluate its work against specific, ground-truth data." The fact is accurate; it should have been attributed to TechCrunch, not Google.
